utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I do understand that we are waiting for the Dutch interpreter but perhaps meanwhile we could deal with a few minor -- at least not very much time, concerning procedural issues. The Chamber still owes the parties a decision in respect of the report of Professor Zecevic. It is admitted into evidence in its entirety. It is not quite clear to me, Mr. Ierace, since one part of the report bears a "P" number, that is P3276, and the curriculum vitae and the two supplemental information sheets, they do not bear any "P" number. Or is there -- or is the report with all its annexes -- well, when you find out exactly about the numbers -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. That is P3276.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Attached to it are curriculum vitae, two supplemental information sheets and the statement of Professor Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that is all part of the same exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it exists of five parts. It's called in its entirely P3276. It has been redacted -- the part has been taken out. No further redactions are necessary and the two supplemental information sheets are, the witness has testified that he recognises them and that these are the -- this is the additional information he gave to his report. So it's admitted in its entirety. Then, I have another issue I would like to raise. That is about expert witnesses. Mr. Ierace is the Chamber right in understanding that through the expert, Mr. Higgs, the Prosecution intends to submit to witness statements, statements that we have not seen before, witnesses that have not been testified in this court, a certain Mr. Kadric and a Mr. Gasi.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The relevance of that is it is information which the witness, the expert witness, Mr. Higgs, has taken into account and therefore, it is appropriate that the Trial Chamber should be aware of that information and of course it is a matter of weight as to what reliance one places on that aspect of his opinion, which depends on that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of the problems of the Chamber might be, Mr. Ierace, is that the statements of Mr. Kadric and Mr. Gasi contains some very specific information in respect of the shelling incident concerned and the Defence has had no opportunity to cross-examine these witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would you allow me the opportunity of discussing that with the relevant member of my trial team and perhaps responding to it later in the day. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so. And then a last issue is about the expert reports of Mr. Hinchliffe and Mr. Higgs. These reports have been presented as reports of experts. The Chamber for practical reasons, announces that it might feel the need after the Prosecution has, I would say, summarily introduced the expert and his report, that we might feel the need to test whether the evidence could be admitted as expert evidence. If so then of course, the normal course of examination and cross-examination will further take place. If not, we might have a gap in the programme and the Chamber thinks it -- we would, having no idea yet on what our decision will be, but we would really deplore it if we would lose one or two days because there is no alternative filling up. And since the Chamber also noticed that as just as the Defence noticed, that some of the experts, also other experts, are working for the OTP. It might be a suggestion, perhaps, to prepare for their presence, if the evidence of these experts would take less time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that Ewa Tabeau is unavailable for part of the remaining four weeks. I will check whether she is available to come in, should it be required, in place of either or both Mrs. Higgs and Hinchliffe. Mr. President, it is an issue which you are in a position to indicate at this stage, the issue which troubles the Trial Chamber as to the qualifying of those two witnesses as experts?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will deliberate within the Chamber whether our development of thought is such that we could say anything more about it. But of course, we are only recently confronted with these statements and it was for practical reasons mainly at this moment that we draw your attention to that. Having dealt with these procedural issues, I wonder whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, pardon my curiosity but it occurs to me that if there is a problem in the mind of the Trial Chamber in relation to both Higgs and Hinchliffe might I enquire as to whether the affects Mr. Kovac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since we neither did discuss that, I will put it on my list to be discussed within the Chamber as well. Can we find out whether Mr. -- Mrs. Eva Bodor has arrived. Okay. Could you please bring in the witness. It would be Mr. Van Baal who will be further examined in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. General Van Baal and Mrs. Bodor may I remind both of you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony. The cross-examination by counsel for the Prosecution will now be resumed. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I indicate for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, including the Defence, that the document which are showed to the witness at the conclusion of his testimony on the 13th of June, I don't pursue there was an error in the translation and as a result of that error, the document now lacks relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we talking about the 7th of June or?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I have the document number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The document number is 1347 I think. Excuse me. I am sorry it is 2753. So I don't wish to show that document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do we agree that General Van Baal was here the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. President. The 7th of June, yes. Mr. President, I will then move on to the remaining document, which is P2840. Could that please be shown to the witness. I am sorry, Mr. President. I think we need to go into close said session for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we need to, we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will turn into closed session and wait for the further distribution until we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now are in open session, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, have you heard before the term, "collateral damage"?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Certainly, yes, I am familiar with that term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what you understand by that term?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It can best be described as unintentional ancillary damage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well the question had an answer, so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you wanted to object then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does a commander have a responsibility or duty to minimise or avoid collateral damage?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In -- generally speaking, one should say, yes. In the situation of UNPROFOR, there were very clear rules of engagement mentioning very clearly that collateral damage was to be avoided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your time in Sarajevo, were there decisions taken by UNPROFOR which involved fire and which involved taking into account possible civilian casualties as a result of the fire?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: As far as I have seen this was always a fairly important issue in the decision on whether or not to use violence. And I have an example myself whereby in August close air support was applied for, for arms systems which were located within the total exclusion zone and were not authorised to be there. And whereby we gave a brief warning to the representative of UNPROFOR with the Serbs, that was Major Indjic. To make sure that the personnel manning those armed systems would be warned that the systems would be attacked by NATO. And by doing so, we wanted to avoid that when these armed systems were eliminated, unnecessary victims would be made. This was all the more important because the arms systems were often set up in residential areas or hidden there. And, therefore, it could be that not only the people manning the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. systems, but also innocent civilians might be hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions on this issue of collateral damage in relation to the warring parties in Sarajevo now, not UNPROFOR. You were on the ground from January 1994 until the end of the indictment period, that is, August 1994, and beyond. Firstly was it the case --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to have a more accurate question, what we mean by "on the ground." Because I believe that the position of this witness was that he was in Sarajevo and in February not in January. See, he was elsewhere in January perhaps somewhere else in the former Yugoslavia but not in Sarajevo. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I stand corrected, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were appointed in January 1994 and you took up your position in February. Were there military targets in civilian areas in the city of Sarajevo, and by that I mean military objects, military personnel, that would be military targets for the purposes of the Serb armed forces?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: As far as heavy arms systems are concerned I have not been able to see that on the Muslim side in Sarajevo the items -- systems were located amidst the civilian population. As far as UNPROFOR was aware of this, a number of the armed systems were hidden under a fly-over which had been closed, but from there, they couldn't be used. The arms systems of the Serbs were under the control of UNPROFOR and were part of Lukavica Works. And in other places, the arms had been assembled but were reasonably separate from the civilian population. As soon as the Serbs got their arms out of the weapons collection points, they could regularly be found in inhabited areas. And they tried to hide them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a hypothetical question. Assuming that the accused, General Galic, was aware of a military target located in an urban area, what factors would you consider the accused as commander should take into account in determining whether the target should be hit and, if so, what type of weaponry would be appropriate, having regard to its location in an urban area, that is, where civilians may be nearby?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a too general question because I think the situation was quite -- is quite different. If we speak, for instance, for the fire coming from Sarajevo and then a unit going through Sarajevo or as perhaps you have seen already in the headquarters which is by definition an immobile target, therefore, I think that the question is asked in too general terms and that it should be made more to the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will rephrase the question to take out the element of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But I stand by the question in every other sense because it is then open to factor in additional factors such as, if there had been fire coming from that area and so on. But in my submission, the question is otherwise not only in proper form, but relevantly probative of an issue which has particularly arisen last Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It always has to balance. If you become too specific, then it might easily be a leading question. But the witness, by now, certainly will be aware that if any distinction should be made between mobile military targets or immobile military targets then of course he is free to do so in his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I will rephrase the question and split it up in two separate questions to make it easier. If a commander is made aware of a military target which is located in an area where there are civilians then in your opinion, what are the factors or at least some of the factors that a responsible commander should have regard to in deciding whether the target should in fact be hit?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: The main element in deciding this is the effect the possible target may have, the influence it may have on the development of the fight and the elements it may have on the development of the fight in the longer term. And the more direct the effect and the bigger the effect, then a consideration may take place whereby it may be inevitable that civilian victims be made. Coming back to your earlier remark with regard to the hypothetical situation, since we are talking from the 24th of February to the end of August, which is a period when I was Chief of Staff, that there was a clear agreement regarding the total exclusion zone of Sarajevo. And generally speaking, people adhered to that agreement. The situation before that was totally different. The war simply went on. After the proclamation of the total exclusion zone, the situation was totally different. So from time to time it happened that the Serbs fired at the city and the same happened when the Muslims fired back at Serb -- Serbian targets. And to what extent they have reflected on and actually prevented the creation of collateral damage, of course, I do not know. But generally speaking, one might say that the defending positions of the Muslims, as well as the positions of the encirclement of Sarajevo, were not being separated from inhabited areas. So, even though during an attack there was no intention to cause collateral damage, then even so it was never to be excluded since the people lived very close to the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, now, in relation to my next question, I remind you that we are in open session. You have told us and we have heard evidence from other witnesses to the effect that there was an anti-sniping unit within UNPROFOR, in other words, snipers against civilians were targeted by the UNPROFOR anti-sniping unit so as to stop the threat to civilians. The evidence is to the effect that the method used by the anti-sniping unit was to fire back, in other words, with small arms, with rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that on Friday when I referred to the -- to some other evidence that we heard, I was told that that would not have been the case. Now, Mr. Ierace is now making reference to other evidence, to other testimonies, and once again they so should not be the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, last Friday I made a point of saying that I did not object to references by counsel to other evidence provided it was noncontentious. If my learned colleague is telling me that he disputes that there were anti-sniping units used by UNPROFOR, then that is another matter. Perhaps he should clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please, that is what the words of Mr. Ierace were last Friday in reference to other testimony would not be allowed if it was a contested issue. So, therefore, could you please explain the position of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am not sure -- I am not sure, as a matter of fact that this was done or this had to do with small arms. I don't know how that came about. And I do not think that that matter is a matter disputed by other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, to save time I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, if a sniper was operating from a room in an apartment building that was occupied by civilians, would you think it appropriate to take the sniper out by, say, artillery fire against the building?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In my view, that would be disproportional.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the information available to the commander was that there may be civilians living in the building, perhaps there were and perhaps there were not would that change your opinion or would your opinion remain the same?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: If there is no certainty with regard to the presence of civilians, then I myself would not like to be responsible of that. I would not use artillery against a single sniper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your answer 5 or 10 minutes ago where you responded to the hypothetical situation that I gave you, you referred to one of the relevant factors being the -- and I don't think those were your words -- but the degree of threat or the significance of the military object or target. Are you able to indicate something of the comparative value of targets, say for instance, infantry soldiers off duty, as opposed to soldiers at the front line or say, a piece of military hardware that had a significant potential for damage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this seems to be a highly hypothetical question. It is not a question about concrete fact, but hypothesis and I do not think that the witness needs to answer to something which is a pure hypothesis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I certainly do not want the witness to answer unless he is comfortable to do so. However, the fact that they are hypothetical situations, I would suggest is no reason to not allow the evidence. In fact, I think it is of considerable value to the Trial Chamber because it is hypothetical. It has obvious significance and relevance, I should say, to the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. The question is about the clarification of the words of the witness that said that the -- that for decision, it was the effect the possible target might have. The influence it might have on the development of the -- the translation says fight, and the elements it may have on the fight and the longer term. The witness used different words, I think, the second time. He was using the word which would be "combat" rather than fight. So, ask for a clarification of this answer, the question may be put to the witness. Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question in my view should be placed in the context of the time, the point in time in the war. At different stages in the conflict, considerations may be made regarding direct interests or -- I am sorry. I can hear the translation in my headset. By the effect in the short time and in the longer term and in the medium term. So that means, if the parties are in an armed conflict that all targets, so to speak, can be attacked at the same time, the situation in 1994 in Bosnia-Herzegovina was no longer a situation of full war. So at that time too -- in fact there was no more reason, for example, to fire at Tito Barracks from the Serb position where the Muslim forces were concentrated and were being trained. And in the previous -- the period prior to that that this happened, for various reasons, and I think because of the proclamation of the total exclusion zone there was absolutely no more reason to fire at those Tito Barracks or other military targets using a heavy arms. The fact is that the war was not over, but the combats had been reduced to a minimum, at least, in and around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that I can understand your evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interfere.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it disturbs you to hear the English translation at the same time you may choose another channel. If, however, you appreciate to listen to the translation of your words into English by the interpreters, then, of course, leave it as it is. If you don't want to hear it, I think -- I take it that you are on channel 4 by now. And channel 2 would be...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you will not hear the English translation any more. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that because of the proclamation of the total exclusion zone there was no more reason to fire at, for instance, Tito Barracks or other military targets, using heavy arms. Is that because the arms were under, that is the Muslim arms, Bosniak arms, were under UN control or is it for some other reason that you say that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: To the extent that was relevant during the period of February, the Muslim weapons were under the control of UNPROFOR. Afterwards, it turned out that some of the heavy weapons were not -- had not been transferred to UNPROFOR and had been stored in a tunnel, the fly-over that I mentioned earlier. In practice however, very sporadically, the Muslims succeeded in placing a mortar or a tank and having that fire, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. especially with respect to the Serb section where 99 per cent of the heavy weapons were controlled by UNPROFOR there [as interpreted]. But the military units still in Tito Barracks could not influence the Serb installations in any way whatsoever in the city. So there was no reason to shoot at the Muslim in Tito barracks either. Into the -- I can recollect that didn't happen in the period I am speaking about of either. There was however firing between Serb and Muslim fighters in which they accused each other of trying to conquer new territory and the Serbs certainly did deploy heavy weapons there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I again interfere. I know that you understand at least some English. Can you please look at your screen page 18, line 1, starts with the words, "especially.". I don't remember you having said anything --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Skip it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was no -- yes, it is an addition to the words of General Van Baal. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. And could you tell us please, when will the break be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next break will be at a quarter to 4.00. And just to give you proper information, two and a half hours was taken by the Prosecution, and you know it is not necessary to take the same time. Then at least you know the limits. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General. General, I will take the liberty of asking you some questions with reference to your statement some time ago and your evidence today. Today you said that you did not truly -- that you did not truly see heavy weaponry on the Sarajevo side with your own eyes. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: You mean heavy weapons on the side of the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On the side of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's correct. I did not visit sites on the Muslim side. The only weapons that I actually saw were in Tito Barracks and they were under the control by the French Battalion that was stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, you mentioned towards the end of your evidence today that there was a tank and some mortars which were not under the UNPROFOR control and which the Muslim forces could have fired, would have fired. What do you know about this tank, that is my first question?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: There were two reports, one of a mortar that was positioned near the airport. And there was one report of a tank which from the tunnel or the fly-over was displaced across the city, it took firing position, and did indeed fire away from the city. Those were the two reports I experienced during my period. UNPROFOR's action was to try as quickly as possible to get to both locations and to take on both these weapon positions under UNPROFOR responsibility, and that did not succeed. UNPROFOR arrived too late.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Would you know more specifically, more concretely where did this tank fire from and when?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely. We would have to determine that based on the reports compiled by the Bosnia-Herzegovina command on the subject. The place was near the hospital, that concerns the tank. And the mortar was close to the airport. I would have to verify the exact time from the reports compiled by the Bosnia-Herzegovina command and I do not have those report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General, when you say, "near the hospital," could you please be more specific?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: If I am not mistaken it was the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General do you know if this tank could also reach another hospital, the hospital which is usually referred to as the State Hospital?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General, the mortar that you speak about, do you know its calibre? Was it 120 or 82?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It was a medium heavy mortar, so, basically a 120 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Because this is not contentious General, we have heard evidence about some other mobile military targets such as, for instance, trucks which have been modified and which had mortars mounted on them. Did you have any knowledge, even if you did not see them yourself, but were you aware of such mobile targets?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: On the way to the hospital in the district near the airport, I will think of the name in a moment, I saw a few military trucks. But I never saw them together with heavy weaponry positioned on those truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say, "military trucks," General, were they the ones that transported troops?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Troops or supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And those were means of transportation which circulated through the city of Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I saw them only in stationary positions, but they were certainly suited for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, General?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that in French, part of the answer has not been translated, "but they were certainly suited for that." Since you are listening to the French channel, Mr. Piletta-Zanin I thought I had to interfere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Mr. President. Thank you very much, indeed. I am focussing on the questions, but thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President my French is not as good and I am still unclear as to what was left off the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has stated that he saw the trucks in stationary positions, but that they were certainly suited to drive around.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not want to have a polemic here, but what is the point of an intervention, because in any case, Mr. Ierace will not going to be intervening in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ierace had some problems in understanding where I added something. But since there was no problem with the English, I think we could have done without. So, Mr. Ierace, yellow paper for you as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, please.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: The district I was referring to was Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is what we thought, General. General, my question -- my question was also to find out if at the same time you did not see these targets that were modified, these modified trucks. There was speak of it during your sojourn in Sarajevo in your circles. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Generally speaking, it is not extremely complex to assume that mortars -- smaller mortars could be mounted on to a truck. This was one of the subjects that arose following the investigation that took place, the multiple investigations that took place, into the mortar attack on the market square on 6 February. That investigation also took into consideration that it was not a mortar fired from a static mortar, but a mortar that could be placed on to a vehicle. Technically speaking, this subject was known.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that at the time of the Markale investigations, the possibility of round or a firing coming from a mobile unit, which was modified for this purpose?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes, this was taken into consideration in the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you. We will come back to this issue of Markale, General, later on. But now, I would like to focus on cars. Is it true, if this is the case, General, that at the time when you were there in Sarajevo, gas or petrol was not freely available for sale since the army had it under its control?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I had no insight into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, did you know whether at the time while you were in Sarajevo there were gas stations, petrol stations which were open to public?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In the beginning when I arrived in Sarajevo in February, that was hardly the case. As the regime of the total exclusion zone started to take effect, the supply to the city improved and increasingly civilian vehicles were driving around, which also obtained supplies at several petrol stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. General, could you perhaps tell us about one gas station in Sarajevo, that, in your opinion was open at the time?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I couldn't give you an immediate answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I thought I understood that you did not know about what legitimate mobile military targets were -- no. No, I did not express myself well. Not "mobile targets" but legitimate military targets. You did not know what they were?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In war, all military targets are legitimate targets. There is no difference between mobile or stationary in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, General. Thank you for this clarification. But what I meant is what did you personally know about, firstly, about their number, and secondly, about the locations of military targets, stationary, not mobile targets?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: UNPROFOR was relatively well and precisely aware the disposition of both material and manpower on both sides including the headquarters of the different military units in and outside the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, I am going to ask you certain questions in a list in order to gain time. As soon as you know where one of these facilities I am going to quote you is, then please stop me and then we can talk about it. Headquarters of the Kultin Ban headquarters of Sultan Fatih; HQ of Kobra; location of what was called Pavle Goranin; location of what was called Petar Dakic; location of Gras; location of Stela; location of Silos; location of Borsalino; location of Caco's brigade; location of Celo's brigade. General so far there is no bells ringing for you here?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I have no idea. It is entirely unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, do you know, you personally and your services as well, where was located the melting works of Sarajevo [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at least the way that is translated into English it is in my respectful submission not sufficiently specific. It is translated as where was located the melting works of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Smeltering factory, interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is a great risk of confusion. Could you please formulate it a bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, did you know if there was in Sarajevo one or more than one factories which were able and had the facility to remelt explosives that were contained inside some weapons that had not exploded, in order to manufacture new ones?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: There were rumours that there was a workplace in Tito Barracks, but I never personally received any confirmation to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General do you know if there were workshops for this purpose in part of town which was known as Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, do you know if, for instance, there was a manufacturing workshop of armaments, of weapons, in what we -- in what was known as "the old brewery" or just "brewery"?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, the same question for the Electro-Technical factory? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, as far as you know in your professional work as a military officer is it true that a location like a workshop for manufacturing weapons, armaments and ammunitions is a legitimate target?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In a war situation definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, the same question in relation to a factory making uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I have serious doubts about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General did you know about a factory that was known as Zrak?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, I would now like to ask you some other questions. You spoke of incidents in relation to trams in Sarajevo. We were on page 6, line 18, for the transcript. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I remember that we discussed this, but if you want to ask me a question about that, I would like to see the precise text again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. It is coming. Could you please remind us of the date of the incident that you told us earlier? The incident that we spoke of earlier.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Earlier in this session? 3 August 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, since you spoke of several incidents, could you tell us if you know of the dates of those incidents, please.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I don't have them at my fingertips. Again I would need to see the file of all reports of the Sarajevo Sector. I assume the Court has them and the Defence has them as well. Another important moment was on 14 August when a child was mortally injured which ultimately led to the signature of the anti-sniper agreement between both the Serb and the Muslim authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, could you tell us of the two dates that you just gave us, that is these dates in August of 1994, were there -- were there exchanges of fire? Was that combat ongoing at the time?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: No, there was no combat in progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, could you tell us if this is true, I think that there is a lot of evidence that we have had in this instance that there were many civilians who were dressing themselves as soldiers partially or completely and they were wearing what we call, "parts of camouflage" uniforms. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In my period, I saw a lot of military troops in the city of Sarajevo itself and they weren't always in full military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, but my question was the other way around. Is it true that civilians dressed as soldiers, completely or partially, that is, just like we have had testimonies to this effect, they would either be wearing top or bottom in camouflage uniform? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I did not observe that, nor did I receive any such reports that it was indeed determined.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will look for a photograph during the break, Mr. President. But this photograph is probably -- should be shown in closed session. We will do that after the start after the break. I will come back to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, how could you be so sure, if you are, speaking of the tram that there was not a single soldier on that tram, travelling in that tram?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I have no reason to assume that there were no soldiers using the tram. So I did not say or I am not saying that in the tram where the 11-year-old girl was killed on 14 August, that there couldn't have been any soldiers in the tram either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, when you were in Sarajevo did you see personally yourself soldiers using the tram as a means of transport to go from A point to B point in small groups?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General Van Baal, may I just intervene. I see that you have something in front of you which appears to have some text in it. Usually, if you want to consult whatever text, I don't know what it is, it is not done unless one of the parties has invited you to take a certain text in front of you. So may I ask you to close it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, may I ask you please to answer the question that I asked you.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Did also people in uniform including soldiers use the trams, also UNPROFOR soldiers use the trams as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. My question was more about, more precisely about the BH forces, as we call them here, that is, does your, "yes" mean or is valid for BH forces, equally?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: No. They are individuals that use the trams. And I never observed, in the many times that I was in the city and saw the trams running, that armed military troops were using the trams. They were people in uniforms using the trams.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say, "that they were people in uniform using the tram," do you mean then that included UNPROFOR people?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Now and then UNPROFOR soldiers used the trams.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, I would like to come back now to the question of what we technically called the "TEZ," total exclusion zone. In your opinion, Serb forces, did they respect this agreement? What I mean is, on the principle there may have been some violations, but as a principle, did they respect this agreement?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes. Generally, it was observed very correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, I thought that I saw in your statement earlier that 89 per cent of the Serb weapons were in the total exclusion zone and that they were under the control of the UNPROFOR forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's correct. Nor am I aware that I said, "89 per cent." It reads "89 per cent" here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that it has been the translation mistake. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I wasn't reading the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you confirm, General, 99 per cent, that is easier to say that, that is what you said, right?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Virtually completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, could we conclude from this that if during this period of time of the total exclusion zone there were accidents that happened, but did it not happen from the heavy weapons of the VRS because they were under the control of the UN?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That wasn't the case in all circumstances. In 1994 in the course of the summer, several attempts were made by the Serb units, not only to maintain the weapons and use them for training purposes, but also to displace them from one weapon collection point to another site, including to a tank war place near Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, I am sorry I am going to interrupt you. When I said, "accidents" what I meant was firing incidents. If there was firing during this period, it wasn't necessarily from the weapons that were under the control of the UN. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question and in view of what my friend has just said, the previous question -- the previous question referred to "accidents." My friend says he is now referring to firing incidents. He should clarify exactly what it is he is referring to. Is he, in fact, referring to allegations that artillery on the Serb army side deliberately or indiscriminately fired at civilians? If that is what he is referring to, allegations of that, then he should say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that we understand that accident and incident are used here as interchangeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If there is an accident which is actually an incident implies that there was fire that was opened, is it true or can we consider, General, that this was not, consequently, did not happen from the weapons that were placed under the control of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the point is this: An accident implies no culpability, that there was nothing deliberate about it. One struggles to understand how a piece of artillery can fire accidentally, but the point is the use of the word, "accident" needs to be further explained in the question. Is my friend suggesting a non-culpable accidental firing or not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am talking about any kind of opening of firing, although clarifying that any accidental opening of fire, of course, would imply responsibility. So, I am sorry, but this is a deviation, now, Mr. President

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... question in such a way, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that since 99 per cent of the heavy weaponry was under the control of the UN, how it could happen or whether it happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. My first question was first of all to have the confirmation, if these rounds were not -- did not fired from those weapons which 99 per cent were placed under the UN control. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see whether the witness can give an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 99 per cent of the heavy weaponry was under UNPROFOR control. The weapons under UNPROFOR control were never deployed. Several weapons systems were removed without UNPROFOR permission and those weapons were deployed, and those weapons were used for firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps would your next question...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Therefore, General, we are here talking about a 1 per cent, the leftover of 1 per cent?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid whatever misunderstanding, your last answer was that "99 per cent of the heavy weaponry was under UNPROFOR control and that the weapons under UNPROFOR control were never deployed, but that several weapon systems were removed without UNPROFOR permission. Do you count them among the 1 remaining per cent or temporarily not belonging to the 99 per cent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your last reasoning was correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In answer to your last question. The last question was: "General, we are here talking about a 1 per cent, the leftover of 1 per cent and you answered that with "yes".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was not the answer you intended to give. I would normally say Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed, but we are at the time of the break. So if there are one or two questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No I would have preferred to have the break just before, but it is perfect now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break until 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would it be convenient at the end of the General's evidence to return to any issue in respect of Mr. Kovac, since he is the witness to start tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I could tell you but without going into any further detail, the Chamber has seen no reason until now to ask you to make special arrangement -- practical arrangement for the time we expect Dr. Kovac will testify in this court. That, of course, the Chamber always has the right, just as every party has the right to test on whether a witness both and what he is and what he is supposed to do qualifies as an expert and whether his evidence is admissible. You have noticed that especially in respect of two witnesses, we have made an observation that we might feel the need and a similar observation is not made in respect of Dr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, could we perhaps return to that issue at the end of this witness's evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We can. I thought that Dr. Kovac it might be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. important for you to know as soon as possible. That is why I answered already that part of your question. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In closed session, you told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not right now, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... indicate that we should turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I would like now in the meantime to ask Madam Registrar to find an exhibit. It refers to one of the tram incidents. Now, unfortunately, I do not have -- I do not know its number by heart. So you cannot do it? Well, never mind then. Never mind. Never mind.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Do you have the witness's name?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well not right now, but I can find it. I think that it could have been Jusic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I will look for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to go back to what we were talking about just before the break, before the interval, would you please confirm that the shots on the city during the period of time when there was the total exclusion zone for heavy weapons, that these shots became rather rare?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At least as translated it refers only to shots. I assume that there is artillery or mortar shots, but perhaps my friend could clarify whether it is small-arms fire or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a perfect question for a later answer, I say "shots" which means "shots."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you asked the witness to confirm something he said before and it should be clear what he has said. Were you referring to go back to what we were talking about just before the break, before the interval, would you please confirm that the shots on the city. So you have something particular in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. I did not ask him to confirm what he told us. I was asking you to confirm the fact which I have presented to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is clear enough for the witness, he can answer the question. If it is not clear, he will ask for further clarification, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The conclusion is correct as far as heavy weaponry is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And, therefore, possible violations of what you have told us would be of a strictly accidental nature?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: They were not accidental. It happened from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Can you -- ask you, General, to be more precise with regard to those "from time to time." Does it mean a daily rhythm, a monthly rhythm and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It did not happen with a certain regularity. The actual reports indicate precisely when heavy weaponry was actually used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But, General, was it frequent; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It was certainly not frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, I would like also to go back now to the tram incident that we spoke about a moment ago. Do you know if after the first incident that was indicated, if you formally protested with General Galic? Did you lodge a formal protest with General Galic?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Every incident that could be attributed to a sniper was picked up by the Sarajevo Sector and they were the first ones responsible for getting in touch with the Romanija Corps and to object to it. I myself have in a number of situations, talked to my counterpart Mr. Milovanovic, about the acts of the snipers as I also confirmed at the previous meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, my question was slightly different. I am referring to this incident. Do you know, yes or no, if an official protest was communicated to General Galic, specifically?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General, will you tell us about the case or confirm that the trajectory of firing at Sarajevo -- on Sarajevo, was parallel with the lines of conflict, the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It was perpendicular to the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I don't know but I am sure if you understood, but I am speaking about the trajectory of the tram tracks -- of the tram tracks in Sarajevo, did the tram tracks run parallel with the confrontation line; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand that the system has frozen, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will then have to wait until it runs again. If there are any new developments as far as the English transcript is concerned... Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the system is back in order. Could you please repeat your question for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall be happy to do that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, General, it is correct to say that in Sarajevo, the tram tracks ran parallel or run parallel with the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That applies to a very large extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And that would include that which is usually called or referred to as, "Sniper Alley"?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General, General, would it be possible that there was the crossfire or cross-shots between soldiers on one side of the confrontation line, that is those towards the south and the forces of those who open fire inside Sarajevo? And that there would be any change of fire between them?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: There have been exchanges of fire between both parties on both sides of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, could it be that this crossfire also included the tramline, the tram tracks?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I cannot answer that concretely from all positions of Sniper Alley. From a technical point of view one ought to suppose that from the Serb positions as well as from the Muslim positions, it was possible to shoot at each other across the tram track of Sniper Alley using heavy arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. In principle and in case of such exchanges of fire, could -- would it be conceivable that some collateral damage would ensue? That is some stray bullets, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Collateral damage where.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Doesn't matter. Does not matter where. But during these exchanges of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question. The question comes in a line of questions to do with the shooting of trams. If my friend is suggesting that shots on trams were collateral damage that is collateral to exchanges of fire between forces, then he should put that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please come to your point, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well that is exactly that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it possible General, in principle, that there was an exchange of fire between the Muslim and the Serb positions which then produced collateral damage during such an exchange?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I can't exclude it, but, looking at the development at the confrontation line and the disposal of the regular units, I cannot imagine that collateral damage would occur using small arms in the environment of -- in the neighbourhood of Sniper Alley. In a confrontation between snipers among each other, these snipers are able firing at each other. And just as well as they are able of hitting any target within that line. But on both sides, a sniper requires a certain altitude and a fire fight between two snipers takes place at a certain altitude and therefore will not lead to collateral damage in the sense of hitting a tram which happens to be passing accidentally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, therefore, I can exclude the possibility of what is technically called "ricochet"?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And why is that so?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Because the distance is -- to specific target is determining for the occurrence of a ricochet and a low angle is all important there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, I would now like us to go to some other subjects, do you know -- did you know about an incident which happened on the 25th of May 1994 which involved two women in the area of Nikola Beronja Street and the Branilaca Dobinja [phoen] Boulevard.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's appropriate for my submission that the question includes something as to the nature of the incident. Was someone shot, was someone shelled, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. It seems that it involved wounding by bullets.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember this offhand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Same then applying to another incident which took place on the 13th of June 1994, a woman of 44 on Ivo Anric Street?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That too, I can't recall offhand. I would really have to check whether I made any notes of this or whether I have inspected these reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, to save time I will give you four dates: 19th of June, 26th of June, 17th of July, and the 22nd of July. Would your answer be the same?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I would really have to check whether I have any information on this. I wouldn't dare to tell you offhand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, but did you ever see in Sarajevo an incident involving two or more snipers, that is, the results apart? I am talking about an incident taking place. Have you -- did you ever see in Sarajevo such a case, such an incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question makes no sense to me at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think Mr. Piletta-Zanin wants to know whether the knowledge of General Van Baal about sniping incidents is direct or indirect. So I think that -- had he ever experienced such an incident himself or that he was only receiving reports from such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that what I understand your question to be? Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never witnessed an incident myself. That is, once I was fired at in a gymnastic stadium when I was jogging and there was a shot fired and it ended up in the tartan track and that was the end of my jogging period. I was never able to establish where that shot came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let us come back to that. But I believe that you never saw a sniping incident during your tour of duty in Sarajevo, am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: You are drawing the right conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General. Did you yourself participate in some of the investigations relative to incidents, that I have told you a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: The sniper incidents, and I presume that you mentioned dates of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. sniper incidents, the investigations were made by the Sector Sarajevo. They were not my responsibility. So I did not take part in those investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Right General. Am I therefore right to conclude that you never not only ever seen -- an incident, but that you also never took part in any investigation of such an incident?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, General. General, we shall now move on to another topic, but before that -- before that while we are still on this subject, do you know, General, who -- in the UNPROFOR, who was interested with such investigation?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Generally speaking, there were two organisations doing such investigations in Sarajevo. It was the Commandant of the Sarajevo Sector. In my time this was Mr. Soubirou who ordered such investigations to be done. And from Zagreb this type of investigation was performed under the responsibility of the chief UNMO. And they were commissioned to the UNMO sector in Sarajevo. The responsible General was General Bastian.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So according to you, General, who was informed about the results of these investigations -- in the Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: At two levels. First of all, General Soubirou was in touch about this with the Romanija Corps and at various meetings, General Rose, as well as myself, discussed this issue in Pale with the General Milovanovic and Tolimir and Gvero as well as with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, these notifications and information, did they happen in written form or differently?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In principle every report made was transmitted orally as fast as possible, but then also it was established in writing as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You said earlier, General, that it occurred sometimes on occasions Serbs were able to fire at the city and that this could happen in response -- as a response to Muslim fire? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: You are making a -- you are giving a rendering of my words. I am not aware that I used these words.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, it may be interpretation, a question of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I understand there's a further technical problem, which requires a temporary cessation of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, do we have any clue as to what causes this problem to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My suspicion is that it has to do with the laptop that the transcriber has rather than the system as a whole. I'm told that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is that if we would have a break now, that we would have -- that we would need a second break as well. I would rather see whether we can fix the problem at this moment well. It seems that -- for the time being, the problem has been resolved. So I would give it a try to continue, but when it happens again, we have to reconsider whether this was a wise decision or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am going to try to ask a different question, Mr. President, to see whether this will influence technical aspect in any way. You said, General, that in relation to the snipers, you would not use artillery against the sniper. Do you remember what you said?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You just explained the technical side of the matter on the height of the firing. Do you remember that, the necessary height of the firing? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, General, now if you do not want to fire at one sniper, but if you would like to destroy a whole sniper's nest, at that moment, would using the largest calibre firing would that then be justifiable?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Quite apart from the hypothesis that snipers in my view never operate in nests or in groups. It is in my view, not right to use artillery in order to eliminate one or two snipers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, I wasn't talking about one or two snipers, lone snipers, I was talking about a nest of sniper, that is, a position from which it was possible to have soldiers in order to fire, possibly, at civilians. Would the destruction of a nest -- a sniper's nest would then it be legitimate, logical, acceptable?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I stick to my earlier point of view that such a location cannot necessarily be eliminated using artilleries. There are other possibilities as well. You are asking my opinion and this is my opinion on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you General. What would be other possibilities to destroy a sniper's nest, to eliminate them?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my friend commenced this line of questioning by referring back to the earlier testimony of the witness. That earlier testimony was in the context of snipers being in a civilian area. I would be grateful if my friend could make clear if that still applies to these hypotheses. In other words, is the proposition that there are a number of snipers operating from an apartment building in which there are civilians or in an empty apartment building, as an example?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as a rule, when there are snipers anywhere, there are no more civilians. If these snipers are acting as part of the army, it is the duty of the army to evacuate them -- to evacuate the civilians. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question is about sniper nests --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In general terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With the absence of civilians. You can't say, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that on the one hand you expect everyone to remove all civilians, because you would not be allowed, which is a normative issue, and at the same time, say I am asking in general. I mean, either you ask a normative question, then you have to make clear what are the data on which you would apply the norm, or you ask about facts and then of course we are talking about facts. So come to your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Article 14 and 15, 4th convention, is it true that the civilian population have to be removed, have to be evacuated?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In principle in a zone where a war is going on, one will try to bring protection to the civilian population, and when it is necessary, possibly evacuate them, of course it is not always possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, if an army decides to have snipers in a tower, does this army have to have the obligation which is Article 14 and 15 of the 4th convention to evacuate the citizens or inhabitants who reside in that building? In that apartment.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: When military personnel want to have the availability of a building for any purpose whatsoever, then it is not allowed to let the civilian activities continue at the same time as military assignments are being carried out from that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Consequently and following your logic, if there is anywhere a sniper's nest officially established sniper's nest, the other side should it consider logically that the civilians must have been evacuated, removed, from that area where snipers are active? From the sniper's nest, itself.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: At the point in time when such a sniper nest is used then it is deemed that no civilians are present. The reasoning the other way around, snipers should not do their work from a civilian environment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General, the question was whether the other party could consider the civilians to be absent due to the obligation of the other party to remove them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Generally speaking, that is what one may presume unless one may be convinced or may suspect that these -- that the people have not been given the opportunity to go away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, now having asked these four questions now, if you wish to destroy such a sniper's nest, let's consider what you just said. How would you go about it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Using snipers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I mean -- don't mean men, I am talking about the room itself, the location itself.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Such a location can only be changed by bombing it. But I said at an earlier stage the use of artillery against a sniper's nest in an inhabited area is not justifiable in my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General there was a team that was established under UNPROFOR called "anti-sniper team" and this team, was it use also against BH snipers?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I don't know [Realtime transcript read in error "no"].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General, do you know if Sarajevo forces or otherwise known as government forces, had at their disposal, snipers, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to avoid whatever confusion, the question was whether the anti-sniper team was also used against BH snipers. It is my recollection that your answer was "I don't know." The answer that appears in this transcript appears "no" and there is a considerable difference. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. The General was intervening. As soon as the interpretation was given to him was "no" as soon as the answer was that he didn't know -- that the witness didn't know, and after your intervention it is now being cleared up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know General if during the periods that I am going to give you, or rather the dates that I am going to list you, were there incidents that occurred, sniper incidents, against the Serb civilian population and I am going to give you generally speaking a month, we are talking about May 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
