utterances.text: Mr. President a question of relevance as to the relevance of giving details to the witness of incidents where Serbian civilians were sniped and by relevance I mean, what is the relevance of that to Defence case. In other words, to be even more specific, is this a quid pro quo argument or does it have some other basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please respond to that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. And I have got perhaps one additional question to you. You earlier asked the witness about certain dates. You said the 16th of July. I don't know exactly. The witness has said in answer to all the previous questions that he might have notes on that. So that it would be possible that it could provide information, but not merely by being confronted with a date and the age of someone who was wounded. So I then was wondering what you were -- what were you establishing to -- what you seek to establish that the witness's memory is not such that just on a date and gender and age he could identify a certain incident or that his -- or that you seek to find information about these incidents or what reports had been made or whatever. Because, as soon as the witness said "I don't know" there were no further questions on that. So I wonder what you are seeking because the Chamber is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, if you are asking me a question and if you authorise me to answer, I will. But if we encounter in these proceedings, if we manage to demonstrate that there were sniping incidents that caused a lot of victims, a lot of casualties on the Serb side, and I would just like to finish --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the first part is the objection of Mr. Ierace, you say it is important to establish and the specific question of Mr. Ierace is, what is the relevance, is it the quid pro quo or is it anything else? Okay. If you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not at all, Mr. President. What may happen, what may be, I will answer before the General, before the witness, in order to gain time. It is not at all a quid pro quo, it is not at all a reprisal this is just established facts. And Mr. President if we are establishing that there were many -- there was much sniping on the Bosnian side and provoking victims among the Serbs and that seemingly, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as far as I know, not a single soldier in Sarajevo was ever accused of any campaign of terror against a Serb citizen, then of course, the logical conclusion would impose itself on your Chamber. Now if we cannot demonstrate the contrary again, we will have our hands tied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, when one analyses that answer, there is no rational proper basis for asking the question. My friend says he wants to "establish the facts." Is just establish facts. The question then becomes, what is the relevance of establishing the extent of the incidents involving Serbian civilians. My friend proposes to put dates to this witness. One assumes from that that in due course, in the Defence case, should we get that far, he will lead evidence as to what happened on those dates. The question is: What is the relevance in terms of the case against this accused? That is what is before the Trial Chamber, not a history for the sake of history of what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that Mr. Ierace would never finish, but I am -- stand by what I said. If people don't want me to ask this question I will not ask it. Never mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked to indicate what the relevance was. And you -- first of all, you were saying that it was not necessarily about reprisals. And then you told the Chamber that if there would have been frequent sniping by the Bosnian side, that you are not aware of any Prosecution of someone not even being accused of any campaign of terror. This is of course a different matter. The matter is not -- although it may be a very important question -- not necessarily the first question to be answered by this Chamber, whether similar charges could have brought against other individuals. So, therefore, that is not quite clearly indicating a -- the relevance of the question. But if there is any other point of relevance, as you know, to a limited extent, this Chamber has always accepted to get a better view on what happened in Sarajevo and this would I would say, also include, as you may have noticed before, the existence of sniping activities from the other side. On the other hand, giving a lot of dates and then say to the witness more or less that if you don't know about these dates then I am not interested to know about it any more, what the relevance of that is, is not clear to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if the General could leave the courtroom for 30 seconds, this time I am going to have to ask him to leave and then I will tell you my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the General to leave the courtroom for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will be glad to. I have had a number of incidents that happened in May and there were civilian victims as a result of these incidents. Now, my question is to find out not so much if there was reprisals that happened, that is quid pro quo is not what I want to speak of, but what I would like to know is if the General tells me, yes, we knew about this, yes we did know that there were many incidents like this. Now the following question would be the one that I am going to tell you about. Do you know, yes or no, as we believe to know that these incidents happened in such a way in order to provoke a violation of a ceasefire de facto, that is all. Now, Mr. President, if I am told this is establishing a fact, which is an important fact that the Serbs who we already heard else where wanted peace no matter what the reasons were but in this period they wanted peace. They certainly did not want war, did not want a shelling campaign nor a bombing campaign. Therefore, if -- then that is what I would like to find out. The interpreter is unable to interpret the counsel's word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot translate these last words.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That I want the shells to fall from your eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said is that we remove the blinkers so that we can see what is in front of us, more or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you want to establish, as a matter of fact, is that sniper fire from the other side took place, and you want to know whether this could have caused any -- whether it was used as a provocation or could be considered to be a provocation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to provoke a violation or a cessation of a ceasefire and to continue the violence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. If you would then ask the witness what you seek, I am referring again to your earlier questions about the dates, but you seem to be not at all interested to find out whether any information could be provided, but you left the witness with a few clues that were not sufficient for him and then you left the issue, which was to some extent a waste of time. Could you please escort the witness into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, do you know if in the period of May 1994 precisely, there were sniping incidents that occurred involving BH forces against Serb civilians. Did they occur, yes or no, and did you know that? I can tell you that this is in the area of --

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I don't remember. I do remember -- excuse me. I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You remember these incidents, General. I am going to give you just a few dates to see if this was as frequent as you remember it to be. 1st of May, 3rd of May, 14th of May, 15th of May, 18th of May, 21st of May, 30th of May, and then 31st of May. I know that you cannot recall each of these incidents, but this -- does this seem reasonable to you?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It sounds high to me. These reports from the Serbs were not processed by the Sarajevo Sector as if victims fell in the city of Sarajevo that -- to which there was free access. What I do remember very clearly is that in May, June, and July, culminating in August, it happened increasingly that there were sniper incidents and that it was necessary to bring the two parties together to establish an anti-sniper agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, since you mentioned that there was an increase, did you know if this could have occurred in order to provoke reactions, for instance, violations of a de facto ceasefire?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I don't know what the intention was of the incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may interfere.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Violation of the ceasefire that means a violation. In Sarajevo, there was a regime of the total exclusion zone. There was no general ceasefire with respect -- there was a clear agreement with heavy weaponry and that was observed very well. But in compliance with the total exclusion zone, the parties didn't manage to achieve a de facto ceasefire between the combating parties with respect to small weaponry, small arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, could we, however, consider that these incidents were provocation, acts of provocation, as far as you know? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Once again, I find it difficult to determine the intention of the actions. We noted that it happened at both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General, I would like us now to focus on Sarajevo. Could you first confirm if this is the case, since we have -- had some testimony to this effect, that the major destructions occurred in the area of the demarcation line or the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General technically speaking, if you have in a civilian area, hypothetically speaking a command centre, a command centre, is this a legitimate military target; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: A command centre is a legitimate target.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, if these command centres are inside the city and on the ground floor or lower floors how could you then get to them?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: By attacking the centre or by shooting at it with artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. When you tell us, "artillery" do you mean by that, direct or indirect fire?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Artillery is by definition, indirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General -- sorry, I understand that the use of mortar, do you mean the use of mortars against such targets, and you say that this would be legitimate?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: For [indiscernible] at command centre the use of mortar and artillery is legitimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, I also now like to ask you something. We shall come back to Sarajevo. But now I would like to know something about some other questions. Of two types of operations, the first one a secret operation which was called Oxygen -- "Operation Oxygen"?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I am not aware of this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you aware of another operation allowing to take explosives in oxygen containers from the hospitals?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I am not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, were you aware of an operation which was called, "emergency" or "container" in which between on the 9th of April 1994, a major element convoy with destination to Sarajevo was intercepted by Serb forces? A convoy which was allegedly a humanitarian convoy.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I am not aware that this was an arms convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know what that operation container was called?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: No I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, you spoke earlier about an incident with Serb troops on the side of the Ilijas Brigade, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That was the operation Citluk with unauthorised weapons systems, is that what you are referring to, yes I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It falls in a situation where UNPROFOR men were blocked for a while?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: After they had gotten the unauthorised weapons under control the Ilijas Brigade did indeed put a -- cordon off the Canadian unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Right. Can you confirm that this incident took place on the extreme, on the outer limits of the exclusion zone?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: The unauthorised weapon systems were within a range of 1200 metres of the border of the total exclusion zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, from where did one start calculating the exclusion zone, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: From the coordinate that the NATO counsel had established.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you be more accurate, General? The 20 kilometre zone, would it be a circle established from its centre such as the PTT office?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: The NATO counsel was very precise and established a grid or a coordinate that was the centre of a 20 kilometre circle. So in the document that the NATO identified to define the total exclusion zone, that is included, and has been provided to the Serb and Bosnian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, with regard to Sarajevo do you know if the so-called Serb parts of Sarajevo during your tour of duty were subjected to the shelling by the opposed side?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: As I have noted previously in my statement, it happened a few times that a Bosnian tank and a Bosnian mortar shot at Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us precisely what was the target?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: The precise target can no longer be established. At any rate, it was a target on the other side of the confrontation line. In the reports that we requested from Sector Sarajevo, we did not obtain the exact location where the projectiles landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Right. General, to go back to what we would like to know, what do you know about agreements concerning the airport area and the territory which was a kind of demilitarised and which was near the airport?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In principle, the airport was allowed to be used for humanitarian operations, and obviously for UNPROFOR as well. And the parties were to comply with the agreement, not to consider the airport as a military object of one party or the other. The responsibility for the airport was with UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only one question, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. President, before the break and after that we will have another 5 or perhaps 10 minutes more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, do you know if the Muslim forces at times set out to use it for military objectives, the factor of the demilitarisation of that area near the airport?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: At any rate, I discovered on several occasions that the section around Butmir occupied by Bosnian Muslims used small arms fire to the approaching planes and the departing planes. And as a consequence of this, on several occasions the airport was closed for a certain period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We usually have the break. I am not quite sure. I would rather continue the second part of this session to take until a quarter to 6.00 so that you can finish the cross-examination and then have a break until 5 minutes past 6.00. So just as in the morning, an hour, another one hour and a half and then the last short hour. Since you would have another 10 minutes approximately. So, please, first, conclude your examination -- cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could then Madam Registrar please show me the photograph or photographs which she has. I don't think it is the one that I meant. Thank you very much. Thank you very much for your cooperation, but that is not what I need.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General do you know an individual who I believe is your colleague, Lieutenant General Lars-Eric Walhgren?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you think he is a man perfectly competent to perform his work?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General I will quote what General Walhgren said for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think the arrangement is that the Prosecution is given a copy of the document from which the Defence puts a quote to the witness. Perhaps my friend has a copy of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that is why we thought that there would be a break. I am sorry, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is not that we have a break at the moment you need to photocopy something, it is the other way around. You have to photocopy things when there is a break. If that would really bother you very much, please continue this very moment and we can also see but under very strict conditions whether one or two questions after the break, which will be possible and perhaps we will then have found the pictures you are seeking as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I will come back to what General Walhgren said in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let us go back to the question of agreements and especially to the anti-sniping agreement. Did you meet General Galic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: No, I did not meet Galic on -- General Galic on that occasion. The ultimate anti-sniping agreement was established and to my knowledge was not signed by General Galic but by the General Milosevic who was acting at the time. That was in late August 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you nevertheless know whether General Galic cooperated in bringing about that agreement called the anti-sniping agreement?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I am not sure of that. From 14 August 1994 Viktor Andrejev attended the gatherings with both parties. I was not involved. So I cannot -- I cannot answer your question in the affirmative. In the preparatory discussions, General Galic was involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: During the negotiations proceeding it, General, was it your impression that General Galic was cooperative?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I met General Galic only twice and that was at the beginning of my period. Afterwards, I never sat at the same table with him or met him in a different context. So I cannot answer your question in the affirmative. My involvement with the anti-sniper agreement concerns the conversations with General Milovanovic and Mr. Krajisnic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, was it your impression, did you have an impression, and I can tell you that we have already heard some evidence to this effect, at what time did the Serbs want complete demilitarisation of Sarajevo and not only an exclusion zone? Is that true, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That is correct, at the end of March, General Mladic urged repeatedly that a ceasefire be imposed throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina and that Sarajevo be demilitarised.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And therefore, can one say that at that time and that is the spring of 1994 and the following months for whatever could have been the reason, the Serbs wanted peace?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That was easy to tell during the meetings chaired by General Rose between the combating parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, does this mean, I mean, for the sake of form, does it mean yes?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, to go back to the latter agreement, we are talking about the exclusion, do you know whether General Galic had a hand in this agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What agreement, Mr. President? Ask the question to specify the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one that we are talking about Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President the only agreement that has been evidenced in the last dozen or so questions are the anti-sniping agreement to which General Galic was not a signatory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You meant the anti-sniping agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I am talking about the exclusion, the agreement on the exclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, both agreements were both -- have been mentioned. So it is now clear what your question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I come back to what I asked you, General. In relation to the agreement called "the TEZ" that is the total exclusion zone, did General Galic have a hand in it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The General has given evidence that he met General Galic twice. I think in those circumstances the question is inappropriately worded. Because one assumes that the answer could only be hearsay outside those two meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Hearsay is not as such inadmissible in the Tribunal as you well know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will soon become clear what kind of information the witness can provide us with. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could we hear your answer, that is, what did you know about possible General Galic's participation in this agreement?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: General Rose told me that regarding the total exclusion zone being in effect, when I joined on 24th February, it was clear that the Romanija Corps was conducive to enforcing the total exclusion zone regime. And to this end, he needed support both from General Mladic -- Milovanovic as from General Galic. That is what General Rose told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, General, can I conclude from your answer -- can I deduce from your answer, that General Galic supported this agreement since he had already undertaken measures to put it into force, to put it into effect. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It contributed to implementing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. General is it true that the implementation of such an agreement does not happen like this or that it is not a matter a few hours, but it requires preliminary effort and very thorough work? It doesn't happen overnight?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's correct. That is why it took 10 days to declare that the regime applied to ensure that all measures were taken to get -- to control the heavy weaponry deployed around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just remind you. You said if we would have the break at 5.30, you would need another 5 to 10 minutes. I know that we meanwhile found some photographs you asked for. There is another document which you still have to copy, and you took 40 minutes until now. So it is up to you what you would like to do. But I am going to keep you to the time limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I suggest that we make copies during the break and then I shall have a couple of questions to ask and that will be the end of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... put questions to the witness until a quarter to 6.00 and then after the break, just the one document you would have to -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. Madam Registrar, could we seek the usher's help to show the first photograph, the first one that you have before you. Thank you very much. Can we show this photograph to the witness. This is 3666. Thank you. Can we just -- P36.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, and could we zoom in persons who are to the right of the tram next to a red vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little bit more, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: General, can you see next to this red vehicle, to the right of the tram, thank you very much, two men? Do you see them?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes, I see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it true that one seems to be wearing camouflage clothes and that the other one has only the lower part of his clothes in camouflage colours?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General, the second of these persons, who could that be? A civilian person or could he be a military?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I can't say if either one, whether they are civilian or military. I note that they are wearing parts of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. And now we have the document and it will be over. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 5 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like the witness to be shown, with the assistance of Madam Usher, a document. In fact this is the document that we are interested in is on page two. This document should bear number 141. But, Mr. President, before I ask my question, I would like to underscore not only the fact that the booths already have this document, but our own experts, our own military experts are in the Defence's chamber, have been there for two hours. I am just mentioning this for the continuation of the proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, General, I am going to read you a sentence which is the one that you have on page 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is, Mr. Ierace --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am not is sure what the document is, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document is as far as I can see is -- oh, you haven't received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. I now have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On page 335, the final page, I am going to read the following sentence which is the third sentence. [In English] "In Sarajevo there were a large number of military installation and, therefore, it would have been very difficult to have made it a demilitarised zone." [interpretation] General, do you agree with this statement that a large number of military installations were in place in Sarajevo, that is the first part of my question?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. General, second part of my question, is it true that this large number of military installations, what should be added would be a rather considerable number of mobile targets like military trucks, cars that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. were used for military purposes, transport of troops?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Ierace, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What do you understand by a "demilitarised zone"?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: A demilitarised zone is an area where all military activities are banned and where in principle, no military and/or their installations can be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You were asked this question, General: "How could you be so sure if you are, speaking of the tram, that there was not a single soldier on that tram travelling in that tram?" You explained that you did not assume that there were no soldiers travelling on the tram. The context of that question and answer was an incident where a civilian travelling on the tram was shot. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the witness was speaking about two tram incidents and since every time there were wounded, could Mr. Ierace perhaps specify chronologically his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General Van Baal, you remember from what incidents you talked about, assuming -- at least, not assuming that there was no military men on the tram?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now let's assume that there was a soldier travelling on a tram and that civilians on that tram were shot, not the soldier. Would you have any comment to make about the appropriateness in those circumstances of shooting at the tram? In other words, would the tram in that circumstance have been a legitimate military target and would the civilian casualties be acceptable?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: A tram carrying civilians is never a legitimate target, even if a soldier was travelling along -- or even several soldiers were travelling on it. As I said before, I have never been able to find, and it was never reported to me that armed soldiers used the trams.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked a number of questions about the significant drop in incidents involving heavy artillery after the total exclusion zone came into effect. What date did you leave your position in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: August 28th, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did that drop in incidents involving heavy artillery commence, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: This happened in fact, immediately, after the total exclusion zone had become effective.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recollect the month that that happened?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: February.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us earlier that you arrived in Sarajevo and took up your position on the 24th of February. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From what you learned as to the recent history of Sarajevo, did the drop in use of heavy weaponry in fact date from the Markale market incident in early February?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: On the 7th of April or rather on the 7th of February, I arrived in Sarajevo and I was updated on the situation, what happened on the 16th. And then I went to the staff at Kiseljak and on the 8th I returned to The Netherlands and when on the 24th I took up my position, Brigadier Ramsey, the acting Chief of Staff, updated me on the developments that had taken place as of the 8th and that was yet unknown to me in the Netherlands. I also checked the reports very carefully from the time of that terrible incident until the time I actually took up my position in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And as a result of your observations and those briefings, are you able to say whether the drop in the use of heavy weaponry dates from the date of the total exclusion zone or as early as the date of the Markale market incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness just said that he wasn't there at the time of the incident of the Markale market. Therefore, he cannot say anything about that period because he wasn't there. The question should be rephrased, put to him differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am happy to rephrase it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, rephrasing would be preferable.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly, what was the date in February, if you remember it, that the total exclusion zone took effect?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: If I remember well, it was the February the 10th that NAC [Realtime transcript read in error "enact"] decision was taken and as of the 20th of February, it was to take effect actually, an actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As a result of your briefing, do you understand that the ban on the use of the weapons was effective only from the 20th of February or the 10th of February or another date?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I am not certain what date I should mention here. In my experience or rather in my recollection the shock of the incident on the marketplace on the 6th had as a consequence that everyone realised that heavy weaponry was to be banned, had to be banned. And to what extent this had an immediate consequence for the stopping of the shooting, the firing at Sarajevo, I do not know exactly. Was reported to me in The Netherlands as well as when I arrived back in Sarajevo and Kiseljak is that there was a fully functioning total exclusion zone regime present. And from the point in time, the NAC had taken its decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you left --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry to interrupt my learned colleague. I didn't quite get the word and I think it is important. I think they may have said enact, but I am not sure. It could have been another word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] NATO counsel. NAC abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: NATO counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that you left on the 28th of August 1994. By then, had the reduced level -- had the use of heavy weaponry remained uniform since your arrival? In other words, was there as little use of it when you left as when you arrived, or had there been a change?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That was a slight increase.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When was that? When did the slight increase happen?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It started after the 5th of August 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now you were also asked whether or rather how should a commander attack a command centre if it was inside a city and on the ground floor or lower floors of a building. And I think you said that it could be done by the use of mortar -- mortars and artillery, that that would be acceptable. In forming your opinion, did you make any presumptions as to the presence of civilians, either in the building or in the vicinity of the building?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I presume that no civilians would be present in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the use of mortars, did you contemplate that mortars would be used against the ground floor or lower floors of the building itself or in the area of the building or both?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That would be a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If the building was in an area where civilians passed by the front, that is the immediate outside vicinity, and the mortar was fired in such a way that it impacted on the ground level outside the building, would you have any comment to make as to the appropriateness of the use of mortars in those circumstance?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question, again, is highly hypothetical. For instance, if we are talking about a building which is -- can be reached by a direct shot, then we know we are in a different situation from if it wasn't in a direct range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I will allow this question and then we are not going to change the size of the building and the number of rooms of the headquarters and et cetera, et cetera. So he may answer this question and then, Mr. Ierace, we reach the limit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it has been determined that the command centre in the lower -- is located in the lower part of a building and the decision has been made to eliminate this command centre, then, artillery or mortars are for good possibilities. However, the point will always be that one should prevent as much as possible that unintentional ancillary damage should be caused, sometimes the interest of eliminating a command centre may be so preponderant that such and so damage will happen anyway. So it is a matter of contemplation depending on the situation for which one cannot establish a general rule. Such contemplation will have to take place every time again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, on another matter, you were asked questions, indeed it was put to you, that the and I think the word that was used was "the Serbs" wanted peace. And you said that as much was apparent from certain meetings that took place that were attended by General Sir Michael Rose. You said at a different point around the same time that General Mladic wanted a ceasefire throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina. Was there any precondition on the desire for peace in terms of the ceasefire throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: There were always conditions to which proposal and one of the conditions that applied to it -- the ceasefire was the demilitarisation of the safe areas including Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And finally, you were asked questions as to whether General Galic, as you understood it, had been cooperative over the total exclusion zone and you referred to something that General Rose had said to you. Was there any other source of information that you used in giving us your opinion or was it essentially or indeed only what General Rose had told you had occurred?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: During various contacts with General Soubirou, it appeared to me that the implementation of the total exclusion zone had been successful only because of the cooperation with the Serbs

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That completes re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Judge Nieto-Navia has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have talked here about the total exclusion zone. But, in fact, I don't know how was this exclusion zone -- could you describe for us the zone, the length, the width, where was the exclusion zone, things like that, just to understand.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: The total exclusion zone was an area agreed to by the NATO counsel in which it was not allowed to have heavy weaponry and the objective was to prevent that Sarajevo could be bombed any longer. In fact the distance was 20 kilometres. And this was intended so that every heavy weapon that was more than 20 kilometres away from the centre of the city could no longer attain the city. Because it was -- since it was impossible that all heavy weaponry that had been deployed, particularly by the Romanija Corps on the high hills surrounding Sarajevo, and to move all of this weaponry out of the exclusion zone and also considering the winter conditions that we were talking about, it was winter time, it was decided that the weapon systems within the exclusion zone should be brought under the responsibility of the UNPROFOR commander. The responsibility for this was the commander of the BH Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Command General Rose, and in conjunction, particularly with the warring parties, he indicated, he set a number of weapon collection points where the parties could transfer their weaponry to UNPROFOR. So the majority of the weapons systems of the Serbs were located outside of the exclusion zone, but a non -- inconsiderable part of these weapons had been set under the responsibility of UNPROFOR at the so-called weapons collection points. And there were some minor weapon collection points but also Lukavica Barracks with the weapons systems they had and the Ilijas Barracks were also considered as weapon collection, arms collection points. So in fact the heavy weaponry could be used no longer by the Serbs nor by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: General, do I understand well if I imagine sort of a belt around the city of 20 kilometres with from the centre of the city?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That is correct. And it was not permitted to have heavy weaponry within that because of the winter conditions, it was decided that the weapons that could not be moved away because of those conditions, to put those under the control of UNPROFOR and thereby, towards, we had -- we avoided that weapons could be brought into the city or that they might take up location from where they could reach the city, to prevent that. The second aim was to prevent the weapons within that 20 kilometre zone could remain in the hands of the Serbs or of the Bosnian army, and could be deployed to shoot at each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Genera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has one or more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] It is again in relation to the agreement on the total exclusion zone. Firstly I would like to know about the definition, your definition of "heavy weapons."

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Heavy weapons were defined by means of the calibre of weapons systems and all systems above 81 millimetres were considered to be heavy weapons. So it has to do with the diameter of the shell or the rocket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So mortars of 120 millimetres are considered to be heavy weapons?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we have had testimonies to the effect that it was difficult to fire mortar shells from vehicles and that in order to do this it was necessary to dismount the mortars, put them on the ground and then again fire them and then again put them back into the vehicle and then go with the car. If I understand you correctly, there was a possibility to fire from vehicles themselves, from mortars mounted on vehicles. Did I understand you correctly or what was done is that they would actually dismount the mortars, fire them, and put them back on to the vehicles and then vehicles would leave?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: 120 millimetre mortar is in principle is pulled by a vehicle. I have no technical -- I have not seen any technical possibility of mounting a 120 millimetre mortar on a truck. I don't want to exclude that it was possible, but I have not seen it. So generally speaking it is correct when you say that 120 millimetre mortar is pulled behind a vehicle or is put from a vehicle into a static position, stationary position and then executes its firing assignments and then is moved again from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, in relation to placing under control of heavy weapons under the UN control, you said that the Serb side had delivered 99 per cent of these heavy weapons in the total exclusion zone so that these weapons would be under the control of the UN forces. And then you said that it happened that later on there were attempts to fire, to actually fire from these weapons. Do you think that those who were responsible for these attempts, did they obey orders or were there just factions that were disobeying, who were not under the control of the military hierarchy, strictly speaking?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: During my period, all I experienced was that all that happened on the Serb side was controlled from top down. Did that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General Van Baal, I have one question for you, that is the following -- no, I have two questions. The first is: You testified that the major destructions occurred in the area of the demarcation line or the confrontation line. You answered in the affirmative. I am trying to understand your answer and also trying to understand the question. There has been testimony in this court that the confrontation line would be altogether some over 60 kilometres. How do you compare a destruction at the line of 64 kilometres with other surfaces or streets or number of building? Would you please explain a bit more in detail what you meant by affirming this, what has been put to you by Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Before I arrived in Sarajevo, most destruction had already been caused by the years of bombing. There was a stalemate, a confrontation line which was hardly changing, moreover the heavy weapons were hardly being used. But in several parts of the city, among others near the Jewish graveyard, the demarcation line still consisted mostly of residential blocks where both parties wanted to obtain an advantage. And all kinds of explosives were used, small antitank, arms, mines and other explosives, in order to obtain a better position of departure by means of destruction in order to obtain a strong position near the demarcation line. And that is what I was referring to when I mentioned the destruction caused near the demarcation line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did your answer also include the destruction that had already been taking place in the city before your arrival?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: No that is not what my answer was about. I focused by answer on the situation that I experienced in 1994 when because of the effectiveness of the total exclusion zone no -- or hardly any heavy weapons were being used on both sides. So the destruction was really linked to small scale operations within the confrontation line and those operations continued and no heavy weapons were used for those. However, explosives, mines, et cetera and that kind of object was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, I would like to clarify one issue. I am not quite sure that you fully understood question put to Defence counsel -- by the Defence counsel to you. You were asked about the operation, "oxygen" and then it was explained to you. And I don't know whether you fully understood what was explained to you. It would have been about transporting explosives in oxygen bottles to hospitals. So, to kind of smuggle of explosives in medical equipment.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes. I understood that but I never was aware of that operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You never heard about it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Never heard about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before you tell the witness that he has answered all the questions, I have one question to ask with reference to one of the questions asked by Judge El Mahdi.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, you were asked about the diameter of the weapons that were covered by the agreement of the total exclusion zone, that is, the calibre of weapons that could be used there and you said it was as of 120 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but this is a translation problem. The translation just said 120 and the question was 82. So the answer is in the affirmative, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but the question is as follows:

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The question is as follows, General, isn't it true that the agreement that I have in front of me wanted to exclude all the weapons including heavy machine-guns starting from the calibre of 12.7 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is inappropriate for my friend in his question to talk about what is in the document in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have not seen the document. Or at least not received any reference to a specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am hiding it for the moment. I withdraw this document that was in my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But is it true, General, that the agreement also included to exclude heavy machine-guns, starting as of starting with the calibre of 12.7 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS PETRUS PAULUS MARIA VAN BAAL
utterances.text: If I remember well, that is correct, with regard to heavy machine-guns, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my friend has been very careful to talk about the intention of the agreement. I for one am now left perplexed as to whether my friend is saying, that was agreed to or whether there was some prior intention to include that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand the question as the agreement to include, so that is not about an intention. Of course, it would have been preferable to present --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... but is the agreement on paper known to you, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would have to check it, Mr. President. But I don't think -- I don't seek to ask any further questions of this witness, if that assists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, General Van Baal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I add something? The total exclusion zone is not an agreement. It was a unilateral decision imposed by NATO which the parties complied with. But they have never, so to speak, in their decision-making, for the total exclusion zone, they have never been involved in the NATO dogma however. Execution agreements have been entered into and there it says specifically in accordance with the NATO document what calibre should be considered as not being committed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since this gives further clarification to your answer, and perhaps also to the question put to you, I would like to -- yes, Mr. Ierace. We have some difficulties in concluding today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Excuse me, Mr. President. I withdraw that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then this finally concludes your examination in this court, General Van Baal. I used to not only to thank the witnesses for having come. For you this would be thanking you for having come twice to the Tribunal. And that compensates that I cannot thank you for coming such a far way as I usually do with other witnesses, but that doesn't change anything at all. Thank you for something and answering questions of both parties and of the Chamber. Thank you very much. May I thank you as well for your assistance as an interpreter. Madam Usher, can you please escort General Van Baal out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that we still have 10 minutes and I think there would be a Prosecution witness, but before that, can I also look for -- go and look for our expert who is waiting --

utterances.text: Mr. Ierace asked a few moments to discuss procedural issues. I have to make one or two announcements. So -- well, for three or four minutes might not be worthwhile to call him. But let's see how quickly we can proceed. And I as such would have no problems having him in the courtroom when dealing with procedural issues. We found, however, a courtroom so that we will sit on the 26th, I think, it was in the afternoon. It will be Courtroom I. So unless other notice will be given to you, we will sit on the 26th of July in the afternoon. That is my announcement. Then, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Firstly, in relation to Mr. Philipps, you may recall it takes a few moments to set up the laptop. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. It is quite a complex piece of evidence.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think that he -- I think he leaves tomorrow morning because --

utterances.text: I do understand. Then the scheduling, of course, is very unfortunate for your expert witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And especially for the Defence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The issue that I wanted to raise is that which you raised at the outset this afternoon, Mr. President, the concern that the Trial Chamber has as to the admissibility of the evidence of Mr. Hinchliffe and in particular, Mr. Higgs. The reason I say that is that the evidence of Mr. Higgs is intended by the Prosecution to dove tail, that is to combine, with the evidence of certain other witnesses in order to form the necessary basis for the conclusions the Prosecution seeks to draw in respect of the first scheduled shelling incident. Since I don't know at this stage what the concerns are that you have as to his expertise, I wonder if it would be helpful if you heard a few words as to how the Prosecution constructs its case in relation to in particular the source of fire for the first shelling incident. I can tell you that it involves evidence from a number of sources, including amongst them, Mr. Hamill, Mr. Higgs, and certain other witnesses. That could be provided to you, if it would assist, in terms of understanding the significance of Mr. Higgs within that pattern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I think this is not the way that we could discuss the evidence of Mr. Higgs and explain why it is important. Mr. Higgs, and I specifically mentioned Mr. Higgs because by the report of Mr. Higgs, two witness statements were introduced or at least are sought to be introduced of which you could wonder whether they would be allowed by the Chamber to be introduced under 92 bis without cross-examination. I mean, experts are not the vehicle by which you introduce witness statements. And I don't think that the Chamber, apart from whether this is the moment to discuss these kind of issues, but I think the decision on the expert witnesses Ewa Tabeau and Mr. Philipps, we have at least -- that is what we think -- clearly set out what an expert is and what we expect him to do. That is an expert witness is a person whom by virtue of some specialised knowledge skill or training can assist the trier of fact to understand or determine an issue in dispute. These are two elements. First I would say the knowledge skill and the training and the second part of this line is that this knowledge, skill or training could assist us in understanding or determining it. That doesn't mean that they take over the responsibility of the Chamber. Certainly there are determinations that are fully to be made by the Chamber. Then we added to that that this Chamber expects an expert witness to give his or her expert opinion in full transparency of the established or assumed facts that he or she rely upon. That is the first part of the is story. And the second issue, the methods used when applying his or her knowledge experience or skills to form his opinion. So we have, I would say broadly, four very important elements, the first one being knowledge, skill or training; the second one whether this knowledge, skill or training can assist the Chamber in determining an issue. For some determinations or for some understanding, the Chamber might not be in need at all the assistance of an expert and that the expert could not better assist then anyone else could do. So that is the second issue. The third is, full transparency on the factual basis on which he builds his expert opinion. And the fourth is, full transparency of the methods used when skills, experience or knowledge are applied, so that we can follow the methodology of the witness that he can explain that, et cetera. So these are, I would say, four important elements that might play a role when we have to decide whether we could admit expert evidence. And I think it would not be appropriate that to go any further that the Chamber might feel a need to further test and rather in the beginning of the appearance of the expert, whether the expert would meet the standards, especially in these respects that should be applied. That has got nothing to do with whether we finally reject an opinion of an expert, or whether we would agree with the conclusions of an expert. That is a different matter. Sometimes even if you would be willing to agree with the outcome of what an expert report says, it does not mean that you are assisted by him or that it is the methods used in achieving to that conclusion would be transparent. But on totally different grounds you might reach similar conclusions. So this has got nothing to do with whether rejecting or accept the conclusions. This is a matter of a test whether the expert is qualified and can function on the basis of his report as an expert according to the main standards I just have set out. That is the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. President, and thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.
